AC Amps to Watts Calculator — Single & 3 Phase | Ampstowatt Guide

Single-phase AC path

Current, voltage, and power factor feeding a real watt result

AC pages need power factor context, so the visual connects outlet voltage, current draw, PF, and breaker planning.

Formula Single phase: W = A x V x PF. Three phase: W = 1.732 x A x V x PF

Quick answer

Use this calculator to convert AC current into real watts with voltage and power factor.

Single-phase AC loads can be resistive or inductive. Resistive loads may be near PF 1.00, while motors, compressors, and HVAC equipment often need a lower power factor.

Single phase: W = A x V x PF. Three phase: W = 1.732 x A x V x PF

Inputs to check before calculating

  • Use the correct nominal voltage for the circuit.
  • Enter measured current or nameplate running current.
  • Use realistic PF for motors, compressors, and transformer loads.
  • Compare the result with breaker and continuous-load limits.

Example: 10 amps at 120 volts

At 120 volts, 10 amps equals 1,200 watts before AC power-factor adjustments. Formula: 10 A x 120 V = 1,200 W.

Best use cases

  • Single and three-phase
  • Power factor correction
  • RMS voltage workflow
  • single-phase AC load planning with clear unit labels.

Common mistake to avoid

Do not use DC-style amps x volts for every AC load when the equipment has a lower power factor.

How to use the result

Use the watt result for appliance planning, branch-circuit checks, and comparison with the main amps to watts formula.

Accuracy and safety note

Calculator output is a planning estimate. Final breaker sizing, wire gauge, derating, voltage-drop limits, equipment protection, and code compliance should be verified with manufacturer documentation and a qualified electrician or engineer.

For the broad formula, reference table, and breaker planning context, start with the main Amps to Watts Calculator.

fx

AC Amps to Watts Formula

The AC amps to watts formula is watts = amps x volts x power factor for single phase AC. For three phase AC, use watts = 1.732 x amps x line-to-line volts x power factor. Watts equals Amps multiplied by RMS voltage and PF.

How

How to Calculate Watts From AC Amps

To calculate watts from AC amps, multiply amps by voltage and power factor. The calculation needs voltage. A phrase such as convert amps to watts need voltage means the amp rating alone cannot produce watts for AC power conversion.

Single Phase AC Power Calculations

Single phase AC power calculations use W = A x V x PF. At a common voltage of 120V, 10 A equals 1,200 W at PF 1. At 240 volts, 10 A equals 2,400 W at PF 1. At 12 volt AC, 10 A equals 120 W at PF 1.

AC Amps to Watts

Convert AC Amps Into Watts

Convert AC amps into watts with amps x volts x PF. For example, Watts=Amps x Volts gives 1,200 W for 10 A at 120V with PF 1. Use PF 0.8 for many motor examples when the exact PF is unknown.

VAI

Voltage Current Watt Relationship

The voltage current watt relationship states that power equals voltage multiplied by current. Ohm's Law connects volts, amps, ohms, and watts. AC power factor correction changes real power without changing the basic voltage calculation and current conversion structure.

Elec

AC Electrical Power Calculations

AC electrical power calculations separate real power, apparent power, and reactive power. Real power is watts. Apparent power is VA. Reactive power is VAR. Power Factor is the ratio between real power and apparent power.

AC power consumption examples use watts and runtime. A 1,200 W load running for 5 hours uses 6 kWh. A 2,400 W load running for 30 minutes uses 1.2 kWh. Portable generator runtime math and UPS runtime watt mapping both start with wattage.

Single Phase AC Power Formula

The single phase AC power formula is P = V x I x PF. P is real power in watts, V is RMS voltage, I is current in amps, and PF is power factor. Divide watts by 1,000 for kilowatts.

AC Amps to Watts FAQ
How Many Watts Are in 1 AC Amp?

1 AC amp equals 120 W at 120V and PF 1, 240 W at 240V and PF 1, and 12 W at 12V and PF 1.

Does AC Use the Same Formula as DC?

No. DC uses watts = amps x volts. AC real power uses watts = amps x volts x power factor for single phase loads.

What Is the Difference Between Amps to Watts and Watts to Amps?

Amps to Watts finds power from current. Watts to Amps finds current from power. Both calculations need voltage, and AC loads need PF.

FAQ

AC Calculator FAQ

Fast answers before you use the calculator or compare formulas.

W How do I convert AC amps to watts at 120V?

For single-phase AC: Watts = Amps × 120 × Power Factor. For pure resistive loads (PF = 1.0), it simplifies to Watts = Amps × 120. Example: 10A at 120V with PF 0.90 = 1080 watts real power.

VA What is the difference between real watts and apparent power (VA)?

Real watts (W) represent usable power that does actual work — heat, light, motion. Apparent power (VA) is the total current × voltage drawn from the supply, including reactive current that does no useful work. The ratio is power factor: Watts = VA × PF. A 1,000 VA UPS at PF 0.80 delivers only 800W of real power.

PF Why are my AC watts lower than amps × volts?

Because inductive loads (motors, compressors, transformers) draw reactive current that oscillates between the source and load without doing useful work. This lowers the power factor below 1.00, so real watts are less than the simple amps × volts product. Only resistive loads (heaters, incandescent lamps) give watts equal to amps × volts.

MTR How do I measure power factor?

You can measure PF with a power quality meter or clamp meter that reads both watts and VA simultaneously. PF = Watts ÷ VA. Alternatively, check the equipment nameplate — most motors, compressors, and industrial equipment list PF at rated load. If unknown, 0.85 is a conservative estimate for motor loads.

HOME Can I just ignore power factor for household circuits?

For most residential calculations, yes. Household resistive loads (lights, heaters, toasters) have PF very close to 1.00. But for whole-house load calculations that include HVAC compressors, well pumps, and refrigerators, ignoring PF will overestimate real power by 10–20%. For generator sizing, always account for PF.

CAL Does this calculator work for both 120V and other voltages?

Yes — you can change the voltage field to any value. The calculator applies the correct formula for DC, AC single-phase, or AC three-phase regardless of voltage. This page defaults to 120V for convenience, but the formula works for 12V, 24V, 48V, 208V, 480V, or any other voltage.
